newsitem.title: IRAN: Total says Sirri project on schedule.
newsitem.headline: Total says Sirri project on schedule.

text.p: Total's project to develop the Sirri A and E offshore fields in Iran is on schedule and first output is expected in mid 1998, the French oil firm's executive vice president said on Saturday.
Christophe De Margerie said that production from Sirri A field would begin in the middle of next year and output from Sirri E would begin in early 1999.
"All that is still on schedule," De Margerie told an energy conference in the Iranian city of Isfahan.
He said Sirri A would produce 24,000 bpd and Sirri E 100,000 bpd.
"Those targets could be met if not more," he added.

Total signed in July 1995 a ground-breaking $600 million deal with the National Iranian Oil Company (NIOC) to develop the two fields under a buyback formula allowing the French firm to receive its costs and a renumeration fee from oil produced.
Total would receive 60 percent of the crude produced over a five-year period after first production to recover its investment.
De Margerie expected drilling to begin in September this year.
He said U.S. sanctions had had limited impact on the project.
"The effect on the project has been very limited," he told delegates at the conference.
However, De Margerie said that the sanctions had reduced the number of companies that had bid for contract work in the project resulting in a "slight increase" in costs.
He said Total also had to improve its relationship with local Iranian contractors so that they could work more competitively.
Under the contract with the NIOC, Iranian contractors have been reserved 30 percent of work carried out at the fields.
